name: @infracodebase/mcp

tools.name: list_enterprises
tools.description: List enterprises the caller belongs to. Use this to find an enterprise_id for list_workspaces. Each row's workspace_count only counts STANDARD-kind workspaces — pass kinds: ['STANDARD','TEMPLATE','MODULE'] on list_workspaces if that number doesn't match what you see there.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description: List workspaces you have access to in an enterprise. Each workspace includes its linked repo if any. Use this to find workspace IDs. Defaults to STANDARD-kind workspaces only — pass kinds to include template and/or module workspaces too. One call returns at most 100 rows and there is no cursor: when `truncated` is true the enterprise has more, so find a specific workspace with slug, or with get_workspace_context and its repo_url or workspace_id, rather than assuming it is missing.

enterprise_id.description: Enterprise ID from list_enterprises.

slug.description: Return only the workspace with this slug. The way to reach a workspace a full page did not show.

limit.description: Page size, 1 to 100 (the default). The API has no cursor, so this is the most one call can return.

kinds.description: Workspace kinds to include. Defaults to STANDARD only if omitted — template and module workspaces are excluded unless explicitly requested here. Pass all three to see the full set, e.g. when reconciling against an enterprise's workspace_count (which counts STANDARD workspaces only, same default as this tool).

tools.name: get_workspace_context
tools.description: Start here before writing or changing any IaC. Returns workspace identity, applicable rulesets, coding guidelines, latest compliance state, and a module catalog summary. Call it with no arguments to auto-detect the repo from the client's workspace root or the server's working directory (the result then carries resolved_repo_url and resolved_from), or pass repo_url (the git remote) or workspace_id. `status` is one of: linked (context returned), unlinked (no workspace governs this repo, but the enterprise's drafting context is returned: when can_generate is true write against `rulesets` and `coding_guidelines` and offer plan_workspace_setup so pushes get checked; when selection_required is true follow `message` first), needs_enterprise (ask the user which of `enterprises` to draft for, then call again with enterprise_id), no_access (a workspace exists but you cannot see it; do not imply it is missing), or ambiguous (the repo matches workspaces in several enterprises; pick from `candidates` and call again with workspace_id). Every non-linked status includes a `message` saying what to do next. With no git remote at all (an empty repo) the enterprise context is still returned, with repo_detection saying why. The rulesets and latest compliance state are scoped to a branch: explicit `branch`, else the checked-out branch of a checkout of this repo (reported as resolved_branch; branch_detection says why none was used and the default branch answered). On a feature branch they come from its latest completed check. Read `coverage.rulesets_source`: `workspace_settings` means no check is visible on the branch yet, and when `coverage.discovery` is automatic a full check will evaluate more rulesets than are listed, so never present the list as the complete set of rules that apply.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, if already known (from list_workspaces or a setup result).

repo_url.description: Git remote URL of the repo (e.g. https://github.com/owner/name or owner/name). Omit both this and workspace_id to auto-detect the repo from the client's workspace root or the server's working directory.

iac_tool.description: Optional IaC tool to include tool-specific coding guidelines for.

branch.description: Branch to read rulesets and compliance state for. On a feature branch the answer is that branch's latest completed check, which under automatic discovery evaluates more rulesets than the workspace's settings list. Omit to use the checked-out branch of a checkout of this repo (reported as resolved_branch, or branch_detection says why none was used).

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The enterprise to draft for when the repo is unlinked and you belong to several (after a needs_enterprise result), or the workspace's enterprise to skip a lookup.

ruleset_ids.description: Unlinked repos only: the optional ruleset ids chosen from available_rulesets (an empty list selects none). Resolves selection_required without a separate get_build_rules call.

tools.name: get_build_rules
tools.description: Read the rules of optional rulesets you selected for an unlinked repo, without reloading the whole context. Use it when get_workspace_context came back unlinked with selection_required: pick the relevant entries from its available_rulesets (rule_titles summarize each), then call this with setup.enterprise_id and the chosen ruleset_ids (an empty list if none fit). Only the selected rulesets come back; the required ones are already in the context's `rulesets`. The response's `setup` carries the required plus selected ids to pass to setup_workspace once the repo is linked. Read-only; changes no workspace settings.

enterprise_id.description: The setup.enterprise_id from an unlinked get_workspace_context result.

ruleset_ids.description: Optional ruleset ids chosen from that result's available_rulesets. Omit or pass an empty list to select none; required rulesets are never listed here because they are already in the context.

tools.name: get_ruleset_details
tools.description: Load the full text of every rule in a single ruleset. Returns rule id, title, full content, required flag, enabled flag, and order. Includes disabled rules (enabled: false) so you can see the whole catalog, not just what's currently active — filter on `enabled` if you only want the rules actually being evaluated. Rule bodies are long: pass detail: 'summary' to get ids, titles, and flags without them.

detail.description: full (the default) returns every field. summary omits each rule's content (the full markdown body), so a large response fits in context; use it to survey, then ask for full on what matters.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

tools.name: list_workspace_rulesets
tools.description: List every ruleset relevant to a workspace — including enterprise rulesets that exist in the catalog but this workspace hasn't opted into. Each row has `effective_enabled` (is it actually active here) and `workspace_setting` (the workspace's stored opinion, null if it's never opted in/out). Use this when you notice code introducing a resource type or concern that isn't covered by any currently-active ruleset, to check whether a relevant one already exists but just isn't attached — then offer to attach it via update_workspace_resources rather than assuming none exists. Only enterprise rulesets that are enabled and not required can be attached this way; required ones are already active regardless. On a branch, `evaluated_on_branch` (from that branch's latest completed check) is what actually applied there; `effective_enabled` is only the workspace's settings. Under automatic discovery those differ, so answer 'which rulesets apply on this branch' from evaluated_on_branch and the response's `branch` block.

branch.description: Mark each ruleset with evaluated_on_branch from this branch's latest completed check. Omit to use the checked-out branch of a checkout of this workspace's repo (reported as resolved_branch, or branch_detection says why none was used).

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

tools.name: get_compliance_evaluation
tools.description: Return the summary of a compliance evaluation for this workspace. With no ref, returns the latest evaluation, scoped to branch if given. Call it once to check the current state; a still-running evaluation comes back with a `next` field, and you should never call this in a loop to wait for it. The response includes a `url` to the results page — share it with the user rather than only reporting the score inline. With no ref or branch, the checked-out branch of a checkout of this workspace's repo is used and reported as resolved_branch; private Work checks from conversations you have access to count, as on every branch-scoped read. A `found: false` names the branch and means no check is visible there, not that the workspace has no evaluations.

ref.description: Evaluation id or commit SHA. Omit for the latest evaluation.

branch.description: Scope 'latest' to this branch (ignored if ref is given). A branch with no completed check returns found: false; no other branch is substituted. Omit to use the checked-out branch of a checkout of this workspace's repo (reported as resolved_branch); only when none is detected does the server fall back to the default branch, then any branch. Reflects the last evaluation of a PUSHED commit on this branch — it will not show local, uncommitted, or unpushed changes.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

tools.name: wait_for_compliance_evaluation
tools.description: Wait for a compliance evaluation to finish and return its result, in one call. Use it right after trigger_compliance_evaluation (pass the run's id as ref) when the user wants the outcome without having to ask again. The waiting happens inside this tool: it checks the server about every 20 seconds and sends progress notifications, so never poll, sleep, or loop around it yourself. In Claude Code a call that runs past two minutes moves to a background task and the result arrives as a task notification while the user keeps working; other clients may block on it, so only call this when the user wants to wait, and prefer sharing `url` when they do not. Returns the completed evaluation (score, result, counts, url) with a `next` field, or, if the run is still going when max_wait_minutes (25 at most) is reached, the running evaluation with `url` and a `next` saying to share it and stop. The run keeps going on the server either way.

ref.description: Evaluation id (from trigger_compliance_evaluation) or commit SHA to wait for. Omit to wait for the latest evaluation on the branch.

branch.description: With no ref, the branch whose latest evaluation to wait for. Omit to use the checked-out branch of a checkout of this workspace's repo.

max_wait_minutes.description: Longest to wait before returning the still-running evaluation. Default and maximum 25.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

tools.name: trigger_compliance_evaluation
tools.description: Start a compliance evaluation of the code already pushed to the linked branch. The platform never sees your local tree: commit and push first, or the run scores stale code while the result looks valid. Pass ref as the branch name you pushed (e.g. 'main'); never omit it (that evaluates a possibly stale checkout) and never pass a bare SHA (it records no branch). Often no manual full run is needed: with CI compliance enabled, a push to the default branch or to a branch with an open pull request auto-runs a full evaluation. After pushing, call get_compliance_evaluation once; if a run for your commit already exists, trigger only a scoped re-check (rule_ids, rule_id, or ruleset_id) for the rules you fixed. Trigger a full run yourself only when no auto-run applies, at most once per task. If the server folds your scoped request into an already-running full run, the response has deduped: true with requested_scope and effective_scope; that is not an error. The call returns immediately with the queued run, a results `url`, and a `next` field telling you what to do: share the url with the user and stop. Never poll, sleep, or estimate how long it will take.

ref.description: The branch name you just pushed (e.g. 'main'). Resolves that branch's current remote commit and records the branch on the run. Do not omit it (that evaluates the workspace's interactive checkout, which can lag a fresh push) and do not pass a bare commit SHA (it records no branch, shown as 'branch unknown' in the product).

ruleset_id.description: Scope the run to a single ruleset. Omit for a full evaluation.

rule_id.description: Scope the run to a single rule. Mutually exclusive with rule_ids.

rule_ids.description: Scope the run to a batch of specific rules, e.g. the rules just fixed. Mutually exclusive with rule_id.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

tools.name: list_compliance_findings
tools.description: Return the per-rule findings from a compliance evaluation. With no ref, uses the workspace's latest completed evaluation. Each finding's `exception` gives the workspace's current exception on the rule, if any. Only `active` is in force: `stale` no longer applies, and `pending` is a request awaiting review. Returns at most `limit` findings (default 100) and reports `findings_total` and `truncated` when more exist; narrow with status or ruleset_id. detail: 'summary' drops the long text fields for a quick survey.

ref.description: Evaluation id or commit SHA. Optional.

status.description: Filter findings by their compliance status.

limit.description: Most findings to return (default 100). When more exist the response says so: narrow with status or ruleset_id, or raise this.

detail.description: full (the default) returns every field. summary omits each finding's justification, evidence, and delta_justification, so a large response fits in context; use it to survey, then ask for full on what matters.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

tools.name: get_compliance_eval_spec
tools.description: Return the system prompt and conventions our CI compliance evaluator uses.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

tools.name: list_compliance_exceptions
tools.description: List a workspace's compliance exceptions: active ones, stale ones (granted against rule text that has since changed, so no longer in force), and open requests waiting on an approver. Use it to see what's already covered before submitting, or, for an approver, to review what's waiting.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

tools.name: submit_compliance_exceptions
tools.description: Submit exceptions for failing rules the code can't or shouldn't fix. Only use this after remediation is exhausted and the user has agreed to the list you showed them. By default every user, approvers included, creates requests that a compliance approver reviews; nothing changes until one is approved. Set grant: true only when the user has explicitly said to grant rather than request. A grant takes effect immediately for the whole workspace with no review, and before sending it you must tell the user which rules will stop being enforced and for how long and get an explicit yes. Required rules can't carry an exception. Needs the user's own sign-in or personal access token; enterprise access tokens are refused.

type.description: risk_acceptance: the rule is genuinely violated and the user accepts the risk. not_applicable: the rule doesn't apply at this level, e.g. a control set per subscription or tenant rather than in this code.

justification.description: Why this rule can't or shouldn't be fixed here. Reviewers read it, so name the specific constraint or design decision, not a generic reason.

expires_in_days.description: Days until it expires. Omit for an exception that never expires (the default).

grant.description: Leave unset to request review (the default, for every user). Set true only when the user has explicitly said to grant: the exceptions take effect immediately with no review, and it fails unless the user holds compliance approve permission.

evaluation_id.description: The evaluation_id from the list_compliance_findings response the rules came from, so each exception is judged against that finding. Omit only when the findings were the default branch's latest, which is what the server assumes without it.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

tools.name: approve_compliance_exception
tools.description: Approve an open exception request (compliance approvers only). Approval is final: the rule stops counting against the score on the whole workspace immediately, until revoked or expired. Call list_compliance_exceptions first, then tell the user which rule, the exception type, the justification, the expiry, and who requested it, say that it takes effect immediately, and get an explicit yes. Never approve on your own initiative.

rule_id.description: Rule ID of the open request.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

tools.name: reject_compliance_exception
tools.description: Reject an open exception request (compliance approvers only), with a reason the requester will see. Confirm with the user before calling.

rule_id.description: Rule ID of the open request.

reason.description: Why the request is rejected. The requester sees this.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

tools.name: revoke_compliance_exception
tools.description: End an exception that's in force (compliance approvers only). The rule counts against the score again immediately, which can fail the compliance check on open pull requests that still violate it. Confirm with the user before calling.

rule_id.description: Rule ID of the exception to end.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

tools.name: list_enterprise_resources
tools.description: Return the rulesets, MCP servers, and workflows available in an enterprise. Each resource has a required flag.

enterprise_id.description: Enterprise ID.

tools.name: list_modules
tools.description: Discover approved company modules before writing or extending infrastructure. Each module includes source_url (underlying VCS repository), registry_source, source_kind, and versions. Versions are the Git tags in the module's own repository, with their recorded commits; latest_version is the highest stable semantic version. Write the source that source_kind names: for a registry source use registry_source and drop a leading v from the tag for version; for a Git source use source_url with the exact tag as the ref. Do not substitute the VCS URL for a linked registry module, and do not invent a version. Before using inputs and outputs, read the exact chosen version from the repository at that tag or its registry entry, never main. Check versions_status before choosing a version: only ok is a complete list; syncing, stale and error are not empty catalogs. Catalog queries read stored data and never refresh upstream, so do not repeatedly poll; last_synced_at reports freshness. Versions include historical tags even if they disappear upstream; version_revisions records tag-to-commit bindings, so use the recorded commit when inspecting a historical version.

enterprise_id.description: Enterprise ID from list_enterprises.

tools.name: list_workspace_modules
tools.description: Read stored module references on a workspace's default branch. Returns call sites, declared and latest stable versions, freshness, and scan metadata. Follow next_cursor, including on empty filtered pages. Never starts scans, compliance, installs or upgrades. Missing, stale or incomplete scans do not prove absence. Local sources have no independent version pin. Latest stable does not establish compatibility.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the previous page. Keep the same target and filters.

status.description: Default all. Freshness only, not upgrade compatibility.

query.description: Search module or consumer names, versions, source addresses and paths.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID from get_workspace_context or list_workspaces.

tools.name: list_module_consumers
tools.description: Read stored references to an approved module from accessible consumer workspaces. Pass a module workspace ID from list_modules. Returns versions, freshness, call sites and per-consumer scan metadata. Follow next_cursor, including on empty filtered pages. This observed inventory is not an exhaustive search of every repository. Never starts scans, compliance, installs or upgrades.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the previous page. Keep the same target and filters.

status.description: Default all. Freshness only, not upgrade compatibility.

query.description: Search module or consumer names, versions, source addresses and paths.

module_id.description: Module workspace ID returned by list_modules.

tools.name: list_vcs_connections
tools.description: Return the version-control connections (GitHub, GitLab, …) configured for an enterprise, each with its provider, host, and account. Use a connection's id with list_vcs_repos and when linking a repo.

enterprise_id.description: Enterprise ID.

provider.description: Optional provider key to filter by (e.g. 'github', 'gitlab').

tools.name: list_vcs_repos
tools.description: Return repositories accessible via a version-control connection — same shape for every provider. Each repo's `path` is the full provider path (GitLab subgroups included); pass it verbatim as repo_path when linking.

enterprise_id.description: Enterprise ID.

search.description: Optional search query to filter repos by name.

tools.name: plan_workspace_setup
tools.description: Read-only. Works out everything needed to bring an unlinked repo under governance in one call: resolves the repo (auto-detected when repo_url is omitted), finds the enterprise and version-control connection that can see it, checks for a workspace that already owns it, lists unlinked workspaces the repo could join, and lists the enterprise's rulesets with the required ones pre-selected. Makes no changes. `status` is ready (a `proposed` plan plus `decisions_needed`), needs_decision (several enterprises or connections can see the repo: ask the user, then call again with enterprise_id and connection_id), repo_not_found (no connection can see the repo: it may not exist yet, or the connection lacks access), or already_linked. Show the user the plan and get their answer to each decision before calling setup_workspace.

repo_url.description: Git remote URL or owner/name of the repo to set up. Omit to auto-detect it from the client's workspace root or the server's working directory.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. Only consider this enterprise (use after a needs_decision result).

connection_id.description: Optional. Only consider this version-control connection (use after a needs_decision result).

tools.name: setup_workspace
tools.description: Apply a plan from plan_workspace_setup after the user has confirmed it. Either creates a workspace (workspace_name + ruleset_ids) linked to the repo, or links the repo to an existing unlinked workspace (existing_workspace_id) and attaches ruleset_ids to it, then reloads the workspace context so you can write against the rules immediately. Check the result: repository_linked false means the workspace exists but the link failed (see repository_error); a `warning` means the link succeeded but the delivery webhook did not register, so pushes will NOT trigger compliance until the repo is re-linked. Relay both to the user; never report an unqualified success over them. Do not call this until the user has confirmed the plan.

enterprise_id.description: Enterprise ID from the plan.

connection_id.description: Version-control connection ID from the plan.

repo_path.description: Full provider path of the repo from the plan (repo.path), exactly as returned by list_vcs_repos (GitLab subgroups included, e.g. 'group/sub/project').

branch.description: Branch to link: the plan's repo.default_branch unless the user chose another. Must already exist on the remote.

workspace_name.description: Name for the new workspace. Required unless existing_workspace_id is given.

description.description: Optional description for a new workspace.

ruleset_ids.description: Ruleset IDs to attach: the plan's required ids plus any optional ones the user chose.

existing_workspace_id.description: Link the repo to this existing unlinked workspace (from the plan's existing_unlinked_workspaces) instead of creating a new one.

iac_tool.description: Optional IaC tool to include tool-specific coding guidelines for.

tools.name: create_workspace
tools.description: Create a workspace with optional rulesets, MCP servers, and workflows. For a repo that came back unlinked, prefer plan_workspace_setup + setup_workspace, which do the lookups below for you. Call list_enterprise_resources first. To also link a repo, pass connection_id + repo_path + branch (from list_vcs_connections / list_vcs_repos). A repo links to at most one workspace, so first confirm with list_workspaces that no workspace already owns this repo — if one does, attach rulesets to it with update_workspace_resources instead of creating a second workspace, since the link here would fail. This tool links an existing repo; it does not create one on the provider — the repo must already exist there (create it with the provider's CLI, e.g. gh or glab, if it doesn't). IMPORTANT: check `repository_linked` in the result whenever you request a link — false means the workspace exists but the link failed (see repository_error). A `warning` means the repo linked but its delivery webhook couldn't be registered, so pushes will NOT trigger compliance until it's re-linked — surface both to the user, never report an unqualified success over them.

enterprise_id.description: Enterprise ID.

connection_id.description: Version-control connection ID from list_vcs_connections (if linking a repo).

repo_path.description: Full provider path of the repo to link, exactly as returned by list_vcs_repos (GitLab subgroups included, e.g. 'group/sub/project').

branch.description: Branch to link, e.g. 'main'. Must already exist on the remote — a freshly created, empty repo has no branches, so seed an initial commit and push it first or the link fails.

tools.name: link_workspace_to_repo
tools.description: Link a workspace to a repo (any provider) for compliance evaluations on push. IMPORTANT: a `warning` in the result means the repo linked but its delivery webhook couldn't be registered, so pushes will NOT trigger compliance until it's re-linked — surface it to the user, never report an unqualified success over it.

repo_path.description: Full provider path of the repo, exactly as returned by list_vcs_repos (GitLab subgroups included, e.g. 'group/sub/project').

branch.description: Branch to link, e.g. 'main'. Must already exist on the remote — a freshly created, empty repo has no branches, so seed an initial commit and push it first or the link fails.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

tools.name: update_workspace_resources
tools.description: Add or remove rulesets, MCP servers, or workflows on a workspace. Required resources cannot be removed. Attaching a ruleset requires the caller's workspace.rulesets.manage permission — a caller without it gets a clean permission error, so it's safe to attempt. When you're the one suggesting a ruleset be attached (e.g. via list_workspace_rulesets), offer it to the user and let them confirm before calling this — don't attach it unprompted.

enterprise_id.description: Optional. The workspace's enterprise ID; provide it to skip the automatic lookup.

instructions:
Use this server for anything that touches infrastructure-as-code or its governance: Terraform, Pulumi, CloudFormation, Bicep, Kubernetes, Helm, Ansible, compliance scores and findings, rulesets and coding guidelines, approved modules, compliance exceptions, and bringing a repo under infracodebase. Search for its tools whenever the user mentions any of those, even in an empty repo.

Before writing or changing any IaC, call get_workspace_context first, on every IaC turn. It says whether infracodebase governs this repo and which rulesets and coding guidelines apply. Compliance gates are mandatory, not advisory. Deliver the change and prove it complies, rather than finishing quickly.

Read the returned status.
- linked: write against the rulesets and guidelines. They are scoped to the detected branch. On a feature branch they come from its latest completed check, and `coverage.rulesets_source: workspace_settings` under automatic discovery means a full check evaluates more rulesets than listed, so never call the list complete.
- unlinked: not governed yet, but drafting context is returned. If can_generate is true, write against its rulesets and guidelines, say pushes are unchecked, and offer plan_workspace_setup then setup_workspace once they answer. Otherwise follow `message` (it may ask for a ruleset selection via get_build_rules) before writing IaC.
- needs_enterprise, no_access or ambiguous: follow `message`.

Other entry points. list_modules finds approved modules before you write new infrastructure. list_workspace_modules reads default-branch module references; list_module_consumers reads their inverse usage. These are stored scans, not your local checkout. Check scan age and coverage and follow next_cursor, even on empty filtered pages. list_compliance_findings shows per-rule results, and get_ruleset_details the full rule text. list_workspace_rulesets finds a relevant ruleset the workspace has not attached yet. A response that needs a follow-up carries a `next` or `message` field. Do what it says.

Evaluations run against pushed code, never your local tree. Commit and push first, pass `ref` as the branch name, and prefer scoped runs (rule_ids, rule_id, or ruleset_id). A push to the default branch or to a branch with an open pull request already runs a full evaluation, so call get_compliance_evaluation once before triggering one yourself. Trigger results carry a `url` and a `next` field. Share the url with the user and stop. Never poll, sleep, or estimate run time. When the user wants the outcome without returning later, call wait_for_compliance_evaluation once; it waits server-side.

For failures the code can't or shouldn't fix, offer exceptions. Show the user each rule's type (risk_acceptance or not_applicable) and justification, and call submit_compliance_exceptions only after they agree. It requests review by default. Grant only when the user explicitly says grant. Approving, rejecting, or revoking an exception needs the user's explicit yes each time.

Always relay a `warning` or `repository_error` from create, link, or setup results. Pushes will not trigger compliance until the repo is re-linked.
